policy: solved = settled by a machine-checked proof or by the curated upstream source (formal-conjectures, erdosproblems.com); removed from the open problems and listed on /status. claimed = a solution has been announced (often by an AI lab) but is not verified or is disputed; kept, flagged, ranked lower and not handed out by default.

entries.title: Riemann hypothesis
entries.summary: Proved by Levent Alpöge with Claude (announced 20 Nov 2026). The Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified on 21 Nov 2026 that both the statement (Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis) and the 17-million-line Lean proof are correct. The Clay Institute has not yet ruled on the prize.

entries.title: Generalized Riemann hypothesis (Dirichlet L-functions)
entries.summary: Covered by the same Lean development as the Riemann hypothesis; formal-conjectures marks the generalized Riemann hypothesis for primitive Dirichlet characters as solved with a link to the formal proof. The Extended Riemann Hypothesis (Dedekind zeta functions), the Selberg-class and Grand Riemann hypotheses remain open.

entries.title: Do Siegel zeros exist?
entries.summary: No: a Siegel zero would be a real zero of a Dirichlet L-function off the critical line, which the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions (proved in Lean, Nov 2026) rules out. OpenAI also claimed a direct proof on 6 Oct 2026.

entries.title: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions (Erdős Problem 3)
entries.summary: Proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 with a Lean proof, which formal-conjectures links as the formal proof of erdos_3. erdosproblems.com still lists the informal status as open until a human reader digests the proof.

entries.title: Extended Riemann Hypothesis (Dedekind zeta functions)
entries.summary: Still open. The Riemann hypothesis and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions were proved in Nov 2026; this statement, for the Dedekind zeta function of every number field, is not covered.

Disputed: a King's College London / Cambridge preprint found that the Lean version does not fully match the written proof, experts question the relevance of the forced variant, and the Clay Institute lists the problem as under review, not solved.

entries.title: A395976 asymptotic (Kotesovec)
entries.summary: The OEIS entry now records Vaclav Kotesovec's conjectured asymptotic of a(n)/A395977(n) as proved by Le Duy Phuc (25 Nov 2026).

entries.title: A337993: finiteness conjecture
entries.summary: The OEIS entry no longer states the finiteness conjecture: it was removed on 26 Nov 2026 after a comment by Jinyuan Wang (22 Nov 2026) on infinitely many k with L(k) < sigma(k) + c*k. Not re-checked here.

entries.title: VP versus VNP
entries.summary: Wikipedia reports two AI-aided proofs of VP ≠ VNP proposed in 2026; not verified here.

entries.title: Tarski's finite basis problem for finite semigroups
entries.summary: Ábel Czupor published on 27 Nov 2026 a Lean-checked candidate proof that the problem is undecidable (235 Lean modules on Lean 4.19.0 + Mathlib, only the standard axioms; prepared with Codex assistance). The final theorem's definitions were read here and match the standard problem; independent human review of the manuscript is pending. On 28 Nov 2026 the proof (adapted to this site's Mathlib, PR 29945) passed this site's Lean checker with only the standard axioms, and two independent reviews found the statement faithful and the problem open before it.

entries.title: Concatenated bounded Brownian pieces (Burdzy's problem 8)
entries.summary: Burdzy's open-problems page links a draft dated 28 Oct 2026, generated by ChatGPT and reviewed by Claude, that claims a negative answer: two stopping rules with every length in [1, 2], used in a deterministic non-periodic order, give a concatenation with no Brownian origin. The author states that he did not check the proof; not verified here.

entries.title: SIC-POVMs in every dimension (Zauner's existence conjecture)
entries.summary: Settled by a Lean 4 proof registered on Palomar on 26 Nov 2026 (PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000040, Hertaspace/sic-povm-lean): it proves exactly the formal-conjectures statement OpenQuantumProblem23.sicPOVMs (SIC-POVMs in every dimension, following Radchenko–Wheeler and Appleby–Flammia–Kopp), kernel-checked with only the standard axioms. Earlier record: Radchenko and Wheeler (Hexagon 2610.00186, 10 Oct 2026, building on arXiv:2609.21892) claim the Stark-unit and reciprocity properties needed by the Appleby–Flammia–Kopp construction (arXiv:2501.03970); combined with it, their manuscript asserts SICs in every dimension. By the authors' account it was largely generated by language models; it is not peer reviewed and no independent check has been found, and a later preprint (Khodaiemehr, arXiv:2611.01524, Nov 2026) still calls Zauner's conjecture open. Exact SICs are proved only in finitely many dimensions (every d ≤ 53 and some larger ones).

entries.title: SIC-POVM in dimension 64
entries.summary: Settled by a Lean 4 proof registered on Palomar on 26 Nov 2026 (PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000040, Hertaspace/sic-povm-lean): it proves exactly the formal-conjectures statement OpenQuantumProblem23.hasSICPOVM_64 (SIC-POVMs in every dimension, following Radchenko–Wheeler and Appleby–Flammia–Kopp), kernel-checked with only the standard axioms. Earlier record: An exact SIC in dimension 64 was released on 27 Nov 2026 by Hayata Yamasaki ('A scalable algorithm for SIC-POVMs', software and data v1.0.0): four exact Weyl–Heisenberg fiducial vectors whose SIC property is proved by an exact Chinese-remainder certificate run on the released data, with no use of the Stark-unit theorems. As of 27 Nov 2026 it has not been reviewed, re-run independently or checked in Lean. Dimension 64 was not among the published exact solutions before (formal-conjectures lists it as open). It is also covered by the unverified all-dimension claim of Radchenko and Wheeler (Oct 2026).

entries.title: Maximal number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension 6
entries.summary: Two computer-assisted proofs that M(6) = 3 (no four mutually unbiased bases in ℂ⁶) have been announced: OpenAI's manuscript dated 24 Sep 2026 (public 6 Oct 2026; the exclusion of four bases rests on a certified binary64 computation, verification package added 26 Oct 2026) and an independent proof by Cárdenes Wuttig and Tindall (arXiv:2611.06917, 4 Nov 2026; interval-arithmetic certificates, with the reduction and the certificate-to-theorem step in Lean). Neither is peer reviewed or independently re-run. formal-conjectures records only the bound M(6) ≤ 5 as formally proved.

entries.title: SIC-POVM in dimension 56
entries.summary: Settled by a Lean 4 proof registered on Palomar on 26 Nov 2026 (PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000040, Hertaspace/sic-povm-lean): it proves exactly the formal-conjectures statement OpenQuantumProblem23.hasSICPOVM_56 (SIC-POVMs in every dimension, following Radchenko–Wheeler and Appleby–Flammia–Kopp), kernel-checked with only the standard axioms. Earlier record: No exact SIC-POVM is known in dimension 56: exact solutions are published for every d ≤ 53 and for some larger dimensions (115 in all), and 56 is not among them; numerical solutions alone do not prove existence. Existence in every dimension is claimed by Radchenko and Wheeler (Hexagon 2610.00186, 10 Oct 2026), whose Stark-unit results would complete the Appleby–Flammia–Kopp construction; by the authors' account the manuscript was largely generated by language models, it is not peer reviewed and no independent check has been found. An exact solution with a checkable certificate in this dimension would settle it independently.

No Lean proof. Part of OpenAI's October 2026 release of AI-generated manuscripts; not refereed and not independently checked.

entries.title: Regularity of solutions of Euler equations
entries.summary: OpenAI announced finite-time blowup for the 3D incompressible Euler equations from smooth data (Sep 2026) with a Lean formalization against a formal-conjectures-style statement; VibeMathed lists it as a candidate and no independent mathematician has checked it.

entries.title: 3SUM conjecture
entries.summary: A preprint by an internal Anthropic model (arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026) claims a deterministic O(n^1.9992) algorithm for 3SUM, refuting the conjecture; its Lean development is unaudited and no independent check is known.

entries.title: Deterministic k-server conjecture
entries.summary: A preprint with GPT-6 Astra (arXiv:2609.15979, Sep 2026) claims that the work function algorithm is k-competitive on every metric space; no independent review or formal proof.

entries.title: Eden's conjecture
entries.summary: A Lean-checked counterexample (GPT-6 Astra, Sep 2026): a polynomial flow on ℝ⁵ whose global attractor attains a larger local Lyapunov dimension on an invariant torus than at any equilibrium or periodic orbit; the statement has not been audited independently.

entries.title: A bijection of ℝⁿ that is connected but whose inverse is not

entries.title: Strict cosingularity and adjoints for separable range

entries.title: Carathéodory conjecture
entries.summary: Conflicting records: Levent Alpöge announced an explicit C∞ convex surface with one umbilic point (Aug 2026, Lean-checked, statement unaudited), which would disprove the twice-differentiable statement, while Wikipedia's list records a proof for C⁴ surfaces (Guilfoyle and Klingenberg, 2025).

entries.title: McKay conjecture
entries.summary: Britta Späth and Marc Cabanes announced a proof of the general conjecture in 2023 (Wikipedia article); Wikipedia's list still gives it as unsolved.

entries.title: Telescope conjecture
entries.summary: Burklund, Hahn, Levy and Schlank announced a disproof on 6 Jun 2023 (Wikipedia article on Ravenel's conjectures); Wikipedia's list still gives it as unsolved.

entries.title: Komlós conjecture
entries.summary: Proofs have been announced in Sept 2026: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, 10 Sep 2026; proof found by the Odin AI research agent) with constant 3√(2π); an elementary proof with constant 36 by Karingula and Lovett (arXiv:2609.20979); the constant lowered below 6.9013 by Akbas and Sra (arXiv:2609.27172); an exposition by Hollom (arXiv:2611.03427). All are unrefereed preprints and no machine-checked proof is known.

entries.title: Beck–Fiala conjecture
entries.summary: Follows from the announced proofs of the Komlós conjecture: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Sept 2026) state that set systems of degree t have discrepancy below 3√(2πt), which is this statement with C = 3√(2π). Unrefereed; no Lean proof of the statement is known.

entries.title: Reinhardt's conjecture
entries.summary: Fei Xue posted a 430-page proof (arXiv:2611.21470, v1 16 Nov 2026, v2 22 Nov 2026) that the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density among centrally symmetric convex disks, part of it by a rigorous finite verification. Not refereed or independently checked.

entries.title: Is the exponent of matrix multiplication ω equal to 2?
entries.summary: Claimed answered negatively: OpenAI's release of AI-generated manuscripts states ω = 9/4 over every field. The upper bound ω ≤ 9/4 is the manuscript of 2 Oct 2026 (family 107), with an independent exposition by Doğan, Lysikov, Sakabe and Walter (arXiv:2611.09716); the matching lower bound, n^{9/4}/2 multiplication or division gates for formal arithmetic circuits, is the manuscript of 24 Nov 2026 (family 379). Unrefereed; the lower bound has not been independently checked.

Still open. One more pair is settled: an AME(9,10) state exists, by a Lean proof of ExistsAME 9 10 with an explicit state in facebookresearch/atlas-lean (not re-checked here). The full classification asked for here remains open.
